name: Low Tide
why: The first song from the sound lab: your palette (your 808 kick, the real hats, the dry hands and wood, FM round, the glass stab, the FM marimba) round an evolving LFO pad. The pad breathes by itself (its cutoff on a slow LFO), and the song moves its tone across the sections: closed in the haze, opening through the groove, blooming in the breakdown, gated at the drop, closing at the end. The kick waits, the bass grows from two notes to its line, the hats play like a drummer, every part's loudness shaped.

sections.name: Low Tide: Haze
sections.why: The pad alone with the hands: its filter nearly closed, breathing on its own LFO, opening a little over sixteen bars.

sections.name: Low Tide: Pulse
sections.why: The kick on one and three, a few hats, twigs in the hands, the marimba's seven steps drifting against the bar; the pad starts to pump.

sections.name: Low Tide: Groove
sections.why: Four on the floor, the drummer's hats, and the bass: two notes on the and. The pad opening slowly over thirty-two bars.

sections.name: Low Tide: Deeper
sections.why: The dorian lift (A minor 9 to D 9): the bass answers itself, the hands answer each other, the glass stab comes in high and sparse.

sections.name: Low Tide: Bloom
sections.why: The breakdown: no kick, no bass; sus2 chords stepping up, the pad blooming open bar by bar.

sections.name: Low Tide: Rise
sections.why: The pad becomes the gated unison pad, cut into 16ths and opening; the hats rising into the drop.

sections.name: Low Tide: Drop
sections.why: The drop: the bass's whole line, the gated pad open and pumping on the kick, the marimba and the glass together, the hats played loose.

sections.name: Low Tide: Ebb
sections.why: The kick thins, the bass in long notes fading, the evolving pad back and closing, the marimba as it began.
